title: How to Speed Up Trust
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article looks at trust as the foundation of effective teams and relationships, and explores how leaders can accelerate its formation without shortcutting the process entirely. Because trust depends on repeated, consistent interactions over time, the author suggests leaders can deliberately increase the frequency of those interactions, especially with new relationships or newly formed teams. The second lever is keeping small promises with precision, since reliably following through on minor commitments signals trustworthiness far more powerfully than grand gestures. The piece closes by noting that failing to honor small commitments undermines confidence in a leader's ability to handle larger ones.
points: Trust is built through consistent, repeated interactions over time and can't be faked.
Leaders can accelerate trust by deliberately increasing the frequency of interactions with a person or team.
Keeping small promises with precision is one of the most powerful trust-building tools available to leaders.
Trust built without a real foundation is fragile and can be erased by a single misstep.
Failing on small commitments undermines confidence that a leader can be trusted with larger ones.
quotes: Trust in relationships, on a team, and within an enterprise is the critical building block of effectiveness.
Trust built without a strong foundation of experience creates relationships that are fragile, superficial, and vulnerable to a single act which can erase it quickly.
If trust depends upon repeated interactions and experience with others, then leaders can purposefully expand the number of times such interactions occur in a given period of time.
In addition to more opportunities for interaction, those who want to accelerate trust often go out of their way to make small promises and to keep them religiously.
Keeping those promises exactly as they were offered deepens trust in a way nothing else can.
If others can’t count on you to take the small matters seriously, they know for certain you can’t be trusted on the large ones either.
